title: Let the depot take freight parcels

blocks.text: The depot's intake scanner checks every parcel's weight and longest side before it goes on the belt. Pallets take much bigger parcels, and since freight was added the scanner still refuses a 12 kg pallet parcel, and the intake screen shows belt limits for it.

`Depot.Parcel` already checks belt parcels correctly. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Depot.java`: the constructor of `Depot.FreightParcel`, a parcel that goes on a pallet (up to 30,000 g, up to 150 cm on the longest side).

When you're done, everything the depot asks a freight parcel, whether it accepts a size and what its limits are, answers for a pallet, wherever the parcel is handled as a plain `Parcel`. Belt parcels keep their own limits. About two lines.

cases.says: a freight parcel refuses a weight or a length beyond what a pallet takes
a belt parcel keeps its own limits after a freight parcel has been made
a freight parcel held as a Parcel accepts a weight and length that only a pallet takes
the limits a freight parcel reports through Parcel's own method are the pallet's

origin.section: A Field Is Hidden, Not Overridden: the Declared Type Picks Which One Is Read

concepts: A subclass field with an inherited field's name hides it rather than overriding it: code compiled against the superclass keeps reading the superclass's field, so a varying value belongs behind an overridable method or a constructor argument.
